subtitle: Mexican shrimp cocktail
verso: For every ill, a cocktail; and for every good thing, one too.
story: The cocktail of every seafood restaurant and beach stand: cooked shrimp in a cold, tangy sauce of catsup, lime and the shrimp's own cooking water, with onion, cilantro, chile and avocado. It comes in a tall glass with saltines and hot sauce, and it's the cure for a hot afternoon.

ingredients.title: The sauce
items: 1 cup of the shrimp cooking water, chilled
1 tbsp Valentina or Huichol hot sauce, plus more to taste

steps: Bring the water to a boil with the salt, onion and bay leaf. Add the shrimp and cook just until pink, 2–3 minutes.
Lift out the shrimp and drop them into ice water. Strain the cooking water, save it and chill it.
Peel the shrimp. Leave a few whole for the top and cut the rest in half if they're large.
Stir together the catsup, [[1 cup]] of the chilled cooking water, the lime juice, hot sauce and salt. It should be loose enough to drink.
Add the shrimp, onion, tomato, serrano, cilantro and cucumber. Chill 15 minutes.
Serve in tall glasses topped with avocado, with limes, saladitas and more hot sauce.
pressureNote: No pressure-cooker version. Shrimp cook in two minutes and turn rubbery under pressure.
tips: The shrimp cooking water is the secret: it makes the sauce taste of the sea instead of catsup.
Some seafood restaurants add a splash of Clamato or orange juice. Every stand has its own.

variations.name: Vuelve a la Vida
variations.subtitle: Back-to-life seafood cocktail
variations.note: Veracruz's campechana of shrimp, octopus, oysters and crab, famous as the cure for a hangover.

items: 12 fresh oysters, shucked, with their liquor
The sauce and chopped vegetables from the base

steps: Make the sauce and chopped vegetables as in the base, steps 4–5.
Fold in the shrimp, octopus, crab and the oysters with their liquor.
Chill 15 minutes and serve in tall glasses with avocado and saladitas.
